ledger.note: 576: Emperor Wu attacks Northern Qi again, by Pingyang. 'In winter 576, Emperor Wu again attacked Northern Qi; this time, changing strategy and attacking Pingyang instead. He was able to capture Pingyang quickly.' The fighting then ran to Jinyang (Taiyuan) and Ye.

ledger.note: 577: the Chen strike at Pengcheng. 'In winter 577, Wu [Mingche] put Pengcheng under siege'; in spring 578 Wang Gui, sent by Emperor Wu, defeated and captured him. The strip itself had been Chen's since 573 and was retaken only in the winter of 579-580.

577: the Qi collapses. 'In spring 577, Emperor Wu entered Yecheng' and captured Gao Wei; the Northern Qi page puts the end at 28 February 577 and says the state 'quickly disintegrated within a month'.

wars.name: Yuchi Jiong's rebellion
wars.outcome: Yuchi Jiong and other regional commanders rose against Yang Jian in 580 and were put down; no territory changed hands.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW. The row (561-586) starts four years after the state (15 February 557) and runs five years past it (4 March 581); 557-560 uses the last Western Wei shape and 581-586 belongs to the Sui (see sui-dynasty_581). The 577 shape (1.77 M km2) is the Zhou realm plus the whole Northern Qi 569 shape; it ignores that the Chen held the Yangtze-Huai strip from 573 to the winter of 579-580, which the keyframes northern-zhou_577 and _580 correct. The strip is approximated by Cliopatria's Northern Qi 561 increment (northern Jiangsu, Anhui, south-east Henan, north-east Hubei), which reaches a little north of the Huai at Xuzhou.
WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT GIVE. The Northern Zhou page has no territorial account (no Shu, Huainan, Tuyuhun or Turkic dates); the capture of Sichuan belongs to the Western Wei dossier (spring 553). The Emperor Wu page does not date the fall of Jinyang by month. The Zhou-Tujue alliance (winter 563) and Empress Ashina (spring 568) are alliances, not vassalage. Yang Jian's rise (580) and the Yuchi Jiong rebellion are on the Northern Zhou page without territory; the rebellion's date comes from a footnote.
PAGE BUDGET. Northern Zhou, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, plus the shared Chen dynasty page and the Northern Qi, Western Liang and Western Wei pages opened for the same state group. No separate war articles exist on the Zhou-Qi wars.
